source.content: Finite repeated game t=1,...,T; round convention is one-based.
Adversary selects y_t in [0,1] and keeps it secret until after prediction.
Player selects x_t in [0,1] before observing the current outcome.
Current outcome is revealed, with squared loss (x_t-y_t)^2.

source.locator: Paragraph beginning Let us start, first three sentences
source.content: Outcomes are IID from one fixed distribution on [0,1], chosen by the adversary at the beginning and unknown to the learner.
If the distribution were known, its mean could be predicted every round for expected loss sigma^2 T; source asserts that one cannot do better.
Expected cumulative squared prediction loss minus sigma^2 T. Expectation subscript names Y_1,...,Y_T, not a separate private seed.
Average expected cumulative loss divided by T minus sigma^2; presented as equivalent normalization for positive T.
Both excess criteria are asserted nonnegative; no probability decomposition is displayed.
Success defined as sublinear total excess or equivalently average excess tending to zero. This is a criterion, not universal success of an arbitrary learner.

The broader deterministic game may allow the adversary to choose its outcome after seeing the learner choice, without a stochastic generation assumption. This separates the adversarial discussion from the page1 IID oracle claims.

source.locator: Paragraph after argmin display, first two sentences
source.content: Future is unavailable; past observations are available; a learner may output the best predictor on its past. This is source support for strict-past information, not an explicit sigma-field model.

source_gap.description: The mean/variance squared-risk expansion and the fact that the mean lies in [0,1] are not proved on supplied pages.
Source omits the explicit nonanticipation/independence argument that prevents an admissible predictor from beating the variance benchmark.
The normalized-total identity and signed little-o/zero-limit bridge are asserted, not proved; inventoried but not a target in Batch27.

No private seed, sigma fields, ae versions, policy factorization, common exceptional set, or joint seed-history independence theorem is printed. These are source-inspired application objects, not hidden printed lemmas.

Supplied page1 gives the variance benchmark but no sInf/minimum characterization. Prove the fixed expected squared-loss minimum is attained at the mean internally; do not claim an expected-minimum display was inspected on a missing page.

nodes.description: The observation map H_t(omega)=(S(omega),(Y_i(omega))_{i<t}) and its comap information sigma field; F_t lies below it. F need not be a monotone filtration.
For each t select an F_t-strongly-measurable representative equal to prediction_t almost everywhere. This is a proof ingredient, not a new public assumption.

Use/prove real-valued measurable factorization through H_t for a representative measurable with respect to the comap. Must check exact factorization theorem hypotheses; no standard-Borel or measurability assumption on S/Y is silently added to target1.

Apply measurable projection/clamping R->[0,1] to the policy on every seed-history pair. Preserve agreement where the original prediction is in [0,1]; behavior on unattained histories and null sets may change.
Intersect the countably many almost-sure agreement and boundedness events to obtain one a.e. event on which equality holds for every natural t. No uncountable-time conclusion.
From iIndepFun Y and independence of S from the entire stream, derive joint independence of (S,Y_{<t}) from Y_t. Pairwise independence alone is not a substitute.
Formulate independence of the current draw from the sigma field generated by seed and past, then restrict to F<=that sigma field.
Transport joint independence through a measurable real-valued function of the history.
Transfer independence from a measurable representative to the original ae-equal P. Target2 requires neither boundedness nor identical laws.
In target2/3, measurable S and Y make H_t ambient-measurable; F<=comap gives measurable representatives in the ambient space. Target1 alone needs no ambient measurability of S/Y.
Use probability measure and a.s. [0,1] bounds to establish integrability of predictions, observations, squares, products and finite sums. Null-set outliers do not change integrals.
Let m=integral Y_0 and v=E[(Y_0-m)^2]. Common law supplies every observation mean/variance; a.s. [0,1] support implies m in [0,1].
Expand (P-Y_t)^2=(P-m)^2+(Y_t-m)^2-2(P-m)(Y_t-m), use independence and integrability to factor the product expectation and make it zero.
For each u in [0,1], expected cumulative fixed loss=T*(v+(u-m)^2). The image is nonempty and bounded below, with minimum Tv attained at m; its sInf is therefore Tv.
Interchange integral and finite sum after integrability; subtract Tv to derive expectedFixedRegret=sum_t E[(prediction_t-m)^2].
Each squared-error integral is nonnegative, so the finite sum and expectedFixedRegret are nonnegative.
At T=0 all sums vanish and the expected-fixed-loss image is {0}; sInf and regret are0. The source uses positive game horizons; this is the sealed target natural-number extension.

An alternative derived proof can first construct the target1 bounded explicit policy and then prove its squared-risk identity, transporting the finite losses back via common a.e. equality. This is optional, not required by the direct representative route.

routes.premise_discharge: Source assertion needs the omitted risk and admissibility arguments; this is not a printed proof.
IID plus strictly-past legal information support the missing nonnegative-excess argument. No current draw may enter the prediction.
Positive T permits division; finite initial conventions do not affect the asymptotic equivalence. Not a Batch27 theorem target.
AEStronglyMeasurable[F_t] supplies the a.e.-equal representative under F_t; no probability/finiteness/IID premise is used.
F_t<=comap H_t lets the real representative factor through the history map, with a measurable factor. Exact library proof/hypotheses remain to verify separately.
A.s. input-prediction bound ensures clamping changes no value on a full-measure agreement event. All-history bound holds even on histories outside observation support.

routes.use_site: T1 forall-a.e. omega, forall t conclusion
routes.premise_discharge: Combine per-t equality events over countably many natural times; choose policies coherently before the countable intersection.
Produces measurable factors, unconditional [0,1] bounds on all q, and one a.e. event of agreement at every time.
Independent observation coordinates and seed independent of full stream establish joint seed-past/current independence; disjoint-index argument excludes t from range t.

At this fixed t choose an F-measurable representative, factor it without clamping, transport independence through the factor and transfer across a.e. equality. T1 itself is not applicable without boundedness.

Establish current-draw independence from seed-past information directly from hind/hseed, restrict to F, apply to the F-measurable representative, then transfer a.e. equality. No policy construction is required.
Same-law bounded marginals transfer moments and give feasible mean; independence is unnecessary for the fixed comparator identity.
Instantiate T2 at each t; integrate polynomial expansion with vanishing centered cross term. The identity is an internal proof obligation.
Use constant u squared-risk expansion, finite-sum integration and minimization at feasible m; prove actual sInf characterization.
Sum risk identities for range T, cancel Tv from the expected fixed benchmark.
Identity plus nonnegative squared integrals; empty horizon explicitly supported. No convergence or rate conclusion.

Use T1 to replace prediction by bounded explicit history policy on a common full-measure event, establish the same risk expansion via joint independence, integrate and transport back. Separate alternative to direct T2/representative route.
